task.title: Sparse range completeness
task.specification: Config length>=1. Start all byte positions unknown. Events put{start,data:[0..255]},read{start,end},clear{start,end}. Put valid only if 0<=start and start+len(data)<=length and every overlapping known byte equals incoming byte; otherwise reject the ENTIRE put without changes. Empty in-range put allowed. Read/clear require 0<=start<=end<=length. Valid clear makes range unknown (cleared). Valid read returns status=complete and data list if every byte is known (empty range complete); otherwise status=incomplete,data=null,missing=maximal unknown half-open intervals in ascending order. Invalid operation status=invalid, data=null,missing=[]; valid put status=stored, other non-read data=null,missing=[]. Output {status,data,missing,known:count_known_positions}. Conflicting data must not silently replace known bytes. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}, initially state=null. Only the current event is supplied; every named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"restore"}. Return exactly the stated output fields each step; opaque JSON state is not graded. All numeric inputs and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; time deltas are nonnegative. Unless a task explicitly overrides this, keys, snapshot IDs, readers and graph nodes are single lowercase ASCII letters. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. At most eight identities and 48 events occur. Configurations and event fields shown below are present. Ordinary regimes use moderate storage and timing; boundary uses equality/empty states; adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events; shift uses smaller capacity, longer timing gaps or deeper dependency shapes, without changing these rules. Generator regimes: Boundary buffer length=3; shift length=5 versus ordinary 8, with incoming lengths and read/clear lengths 0..6 instead of 0..4, increasing overlap and out-of-range pressure. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Dendrochronology
matchedCard.relation: Overlapping sequences can be aligned by distinctive patterns spanning several observations. Cross-comparison can reveal missing or extra local observations that a simple position count would treat as elapsed intervals.
assumptions: The sequences share a comparable underlying history.
The overlap contains enough distinguishing structure to support alignment.
matchedCard.boundary: Repeated patterns or insufficient overlap can support several alignments. A single coincident observation does not establish a unique chronological match.
matchedCard.source_fact: NOAA describes crossdating tree-ring patterns from several trees to account for missing or extra rings and align samples from different periods.

shuffledCard.label: Comparator hysteresis
shuffledCard.relation: A state-dependent comparator uses distinct upper and lower transition thresholds. Between them, the existing state is retained. Fluctuations that remain within this interval need not cause repeated switching.
assumptions: The output has a preceding state.
Distinct thresholds are appropriate to the signal range and acceptable response delay.
shuffledCard.boundary: A wider separation can postpone response to a real change. Behavior with two state-dependent thresholds differs from reacting to every crossing of one fixed threshold.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Texas Instruments describes an inverting comparator with upper and lower hysteresis thresholds to reduce unwanted transitions caused by noise or slow-moving signals.

initial.explanation: Track each byte as either null (unknown) or its stored value. A put is transactional: validate bounds and all overlaps before writing. Reads derive completeness and maximal unknown runs; clears null their range. The alternative of applying non-conflicting portions of a put fails on the overlapping-conflict example because the entire operation must be rejected.
initial.mapping: The state array maps byte positions to known values or null. known is its non-null count; missing is the maximal contiguous null intervals within a requested read.
initial.assumptions: Inputs follow the stated legal JSON contract and config.length is a safe positive integer.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let a=Array(input.config.length).fill(null);for(let k=0;k<output.length;k++){let e=input.events[k],o=output[k],n=a.length,ok=true;if(e.type==='put'){ok=Number.isSafeInteger(e.start)&&e.start>=0&&e.start+e.data.length<=n;if(ok)for(let i=0;i<e.data.length;i++)if(a[e.start+i]!==null&&a[e.start+i]!==e.data[i])ok=false;if(ok)for(let i=0;i<e.data.length;i++)a[e.start+i]=e.data[i]}else if(e.type==='read'||e.type==='clear'){ok=Number.isSafeInteger(e.start)&&Number.isSafeInteger(e.end)&&e.start>=0&&e.start<=e.end&&e.end<=n;if(ok&&e.type==='clear')for(let i=e.start;i<e.end;i++)a[i]=null}let c=a.reduce((x,v)=>x+(v!==null),0),d=null,m=[];if(e.type==='read'&&ok){let full=true;for(let i=e.start;i<e.end;i++)if(a[i]===null)full=false;if(full)d=a.slice(e.start,e.end);else{d=null;let i=e.start;while(i<e.end){while(i<e.end&&a[i]!==null)i++;let s=i;while(i<e.end&&a[i]===null)i++;if(s<i)m.push([s,i])}}}let z=e.type==='put'?(ok?['stored',null,[]]:['invalid',null,[]]):e.type==='clear'?(ok?['cleared',null,[]]:['invalid',null,[]]):e.type==='read'?(ok?[d===null?'incomplete':'complete',d,m]:['invalid',null,[]]):['invalid',null,[]];if(JSON.stringify(o)!==JSON.stringify({status:z[0],data:z[1],missing:z[2],known:c}))return false}return true}

final.explanation: The implementation stores one entry per byte, using null for unknown. Put operations validate bounds and every overlapping known byte before mutating, so conflicts reject the entire operation. Reads report complete data or maximal unknown intervals; clears make a valid range unknown. Each response recomputes the known-byte count and includes exactly the required output fields.

initial.mapping: Buffer positions map to state array entries: null means unknown, and 0..255 means known byte. known is the count of non-null entries.
initial.assumptions: Inputs use the specified event shapes and safe integers. Initial null state denotes a fresh buffer; subsequently returned arrays are passed back unchanged.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var a=Array(input.config.length).fill(null),n=0;for(var k=0;k<input.events.length;k++){var e=input.events[k],d=null,m=[],s='invalid',t=e.type,x=e.start,y=e.end,i;if(t==='put'&&Array.isArray(e.data)&&Number.isInteger(x)&&x>=0&&x+e.data.length<=a.length){var ok=true;for(i=0;i<e.data.length;i++)if(a[x+i]!==null&&a[x+i]!==e.data[i])ok=false;if(ok){for(i=0;i<e.data.length;i++)if(a[x+i]===null){a[x+i]=e.data[i];n++}s='stored'}}else if((t==='read'||t==='clear')&&Number.isInteger(x)&&Number.isInteger(y)&&x>=0&&x<=y&&y<=a.length){if(t==='clear'){for(i=x;i<y;i++)if(a[i]!==null){a[i]=null;n--}s='cleared'}else{var q=x;while(q<y){if(a[q]===null){var z=q;while(z<y&&a[z]===null)z++;m.push([q,z]);q=z}else q++}if(!m.length){s='complete';d=a.slice(x,y)}}}var r={status:s,data:d,missing:m,known:n};if(JSON.stringify(r)!==JSON.stringify(output[k]))return false}return true}

initial.explanation: Track each byte as either unknown or a known numeric value. Puts are transactional: validate bounds and all known overlaps before writing. Reads report maximal unknown runs; clears erase the selected range.
initial.mapping: The buffer positions are the target state, known count is derived from them, and each event maps directly to one state transition and output status. Comparator hysteresis is not applicable.
initial.assumptions: Inputs follow the stated legal JSON contract and use the specified event shapes, safe integers, and byte ranges.
initial.holds: function(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(var i=0;i<output.length;i++){var o=output[i];if(!o||!('status'in o)||!('data'in o)||!('missing'in o)||!('known'in o)||!Array.isArray(o.missing)||typeof o.known!=='number')return false;if((o.status==='stored'||o.status==='cleared')&&o.data!==null)return false;if(o.status==='invalid'&&(o.data!==null||o.missing.length))return false;if(o.status==='complete'&&o.data===null)return false;if(o.status==='incomplete'&&o.data!==null)return false}return true}

Puts validate bounds, byte values, and every known overlap before mutating, so rejected puts are transactional. Reads compute maximal unknown intervals and return bytes only when complete; clears erase valid ranges. Each output includes the current known-byte count.
